bear_case: The bull setup for July 6 portfolio activation rests on conditions that have NOT all resolved. (1) IBIT Gate 3: if IBIT reports another daily outflow on July 6 (extending its 10-day streak to day 11+), the BTC re-entry framework does NOT activate regardless of Gate 2 confirmation — this would leave the framework stranded in cash while BTC potentially moves from $63,000 toward $65,000 without a trigger. Prior briefs' incorrect characterization of an 'IBIT inflow streak' (when IBIT specifically was outflowing) means the Gate 3 setup is less clear than the morning brief implied. (2) NVDA Stop Day 2: the $194.83 OTC carry is only $1.13 above the $193.70 July 2 official close; if NVDA opens July 6 below $193 on negative weekend news and closes below $195, Stop Day 2 triggers mandatory exit July 7 — the same day as SPCX's $4.3B inclusion-day spike creates a chaotic exit environment for any forced equity selling. (3) ES gap-down scenario: Sunday evening ES futures reopen; any geopolitical shock (Iran ceasefire breach, Taiwan Strait incident, G7 trade escalation) between now and Sunday 6 PM ET could drive ES below 7,460, invalidating SPX Gate 1 simultaneously. (4) BTC's $63,015 was achieved in holiday-thin crypto markets — when US institutional trading resumes July 6, profit-takers may sell the Gate 2 confirmation, pulling BTC from $63,000 back toward $62,000–$61,500 before IBIT even has a chance to confirm Gate 3. A 'Gate 2 confirmed but BTC immediately retreats on US institutional open' is the most dangerous sequence for the re-entry framework.
